glossary_audits.name: genocide
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Corrected the definition to require specified acts and intent directed at a protected group. The new examples are illustrative; identification of an act alone cannot establish intent.

latest_context_review.finding: Convention-based definition requires both specified acts and group-directed intent. Its examples are expressly nonexhaustive. Assigned only to the Holocaust case; it does not automatically adjudicate other atrocities in the corpus.

glossary_audits.name: primary source
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Retained the later oral-history and memoir examples, which are essential for Partition. Changed the visible name to two words while preserving the link ID.

latest_context_review.finding: Later memoirs and oral histories remain possible primary evidence. Treaty text, photograph, testimony and translation have separate authorship and mediation; the definition does not make later interpretations original agreements.

glossary_audits.name: patronage
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Ming and Mughal works illustrate commissioning and support. A patron’s role leaves the number and identities of individual makers open.

latest_context_review.finding: Support and commissions fit the Mughal, Song and Bukhara examples. A patron does not identify every maker or establish uniform access to court institutions.

glossary_audits.name: tomb
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Han tomb material is associated with people who arranged burial as well as the deceased. The qualification about whose beliefs the objects reflect is important.

latest_context_review.finding: Han and Tang burial objects are distinguished from surviving occupied houses. Egyptian tomb imagery is not treated as a direct census of living workers.

glossary_audits.name: estate
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: In the Han entry, land, buildings and associated labor are concrete references for the model. Its depiction does not supply an owner’s balance sheet.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned only to the Han architectural-model dossier. The model supports an inquiry into property and provisioning, not measured estate accounts or a universal European tenure category.

glossary_audits.name: afterlife
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Han and Egyptian examples require attribution of beliefs to particular settings. The definition makes their historical representation open to study.

latest_context_review.finding: The Egyptian and Kushite examples concern attributed funerary expectations. No assertion is made that all people shared an elite object's beliefs.

glossary_audits.name: evidence
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Broadened the examples to include spoken testimony alongside written records and objects. This fits living community accounts as well as excavated material.

latest_context_review.finding: Written records, material evidence and spoken testimony remain included. Community sources are not demoted to illustration; evidence still requires attribution and context.

glossary_audits.name: inference
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Colima’s selected figures support descriptions and interpretations with different levels of certainty. The definition uses that distinction directly.

latest_context_review.finding: The Chaco ingredient inference and Ocmulgee seating interpretation remain distinct from observation. Many assignments use the concept without this exact word, so the word list supplies access.

glossary_audits.name: chronology
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Caral and Colima use different kinds of date ranges. The short definition allows both revised dates and uncertain ordering.

latest_context_review.finding: The Kushan chronology discrepancy, Caral date contexts and Polynesian revisions are retained rather than collapsed into exact single dates.

glossary_audits.name: ritual
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Repetition and shared meaning offer a starting point for Colima; shape alone cannot identify a particular act or belief.

latest_context_review.finding: Shang elite practice, Moche regional gatherings and Colima miniature interpretations are not equated. Repeated or meaningful action does not establish one belief or political institution.

glossary_audits.name: dynasty
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: A line of rulers is intelligible in imperial China and Mughal history. The family frame leaves room for conflict and changing institutions.

latest_context_review.finding: Named ruling sequences are distinguished from the whole population. Tang changes and the Abbasid object's broad range resist treating a dynasty as a uniform social period.

glossary_audits.name: empire
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Diverse subjects and unequal power fit the Roman example; the word “often” avoids requiring identical conquest or government in every case.

latest_context_review.finding: Roman institutions and Mali's wider claims operate at different scales. The definition allows unequal control without assigning identical administration to every empire.

glossary_audits.name: freedman
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Roman use is appropriately gendered and identifies a previous legal status. It gives no automatic entitlement to citizenship, wealth or office.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned only to the Roman Eutyches portrait context, where the inscription's reading remains qualified. It is not linked to Cherokee Freedmen, whose collective citizenship history would require a different contextual account.

glossary_audits.name: caravan
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Traveling together explains overland transport at Palmyra. It does not prescribe one animal species or a complete route for an individual object.

latest_context_review.finding: Palmyra distinguishes family memorials from honorific caravan inscriptions. Neither the definition nor the dossier assigns a particular journey to an unconnected object.

glossary_audits.name: inscription
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Words on a surface are identifiable on the Palmyra stone and the Kushan coin. A claim in an inscription still has an author and audience.

latest_context_review.finding: Public, funerary, royal and administrative writing retain distinct purposes. The Kushan dossier distinguishes events narrated from the later production of the inscription.

glossary_audits.name: coinage
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Issuing and using coins connects the Kushan object with an authority and users without treating circulation as a border map.

latest_context_review.finding: The Kushan coin is evidence for issuing and circulation practices; it does not map political borders or prove every person's use of money.

glossary_audits.name: provenance
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The core ownership-history meaning fits the museum examples; it leaves the archaeological findspot as a separate question. Dimensions such as loans or custody may also matter in particular cases.

latest_context_review.finding: Corrected an overly narrow ownership-only definition. Getty includes origin and earlier locations; AIA distinguishes archaeological provenience, and NPS distinguishes precise find location from ownership. Ojibwe photographic-location usage now fits without equating an ownership chain with a secure excavation context.

glossary_audits.name: port
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The definition accommodates coastal and river connections and the transfer of both people and goods. A port name alone cannot trace an individual vessel.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned to Aksum, the Portuguese voyage, Manila and Uluburun. Exact matching does not annotate the letters in transport, support or reported. Landing and exchange are distinct from reconstructing a complete itinerary.

glossary_audits.name: stele
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The simple upright-monument description fits Aksum. Carving and writing are possible features rather than required features.

latest_context_review.finding: The upright-monument sense is limited to Aksum. Writing is optional in the definition, so it does not require every monument to carry an inscription.

glossary_audits.name: archaeology
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Material remains together with their contexts encompass tools, architecture and deposits in Colima and Moche. This avoids equating archaeology with collecting objects.

latest_context_review.finding: Material remains are interpreted with contexts, sampling and chronology. The Lapita discussion keeps linguistic inference and archaeological categories separate.

glossary_audits.name: irrigation
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Directing water to fields fits the agricultural examples. Household water storage or an urban drain requires separate functional evidence.

latest_context_review.finding: Field watering is distinct from household storage and urban drainage. Dholavira's word-list assignment is background vocabulary, not an inline claim that its reservoirs irrigated particular fields.

glossary_audits.name: tribute
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Goods and labor under political demand are both possible in the Moche inquiry. The generic definition does not establish who owed what in that setting.

latest_context_review.finding: Moche explicitly leaves tribute, gifts and negotiated exchange as competing explanations. The glossary does not settle that archaeological question.

glossary_audits.name: iconography
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The term explains how subjects in an image are interpreted in context. The Moche example requires separate evidence for which figure or action is shown.

latest_context_review.finding: Image interpretation remains context-dependent in Moche, Mughal and Byzantine assignments. Formal similarity does not establish identical meaning or use.

glossary_audits.name: regalia
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Rank, office and authority describe what the Benin example can communicate. Possession or resemblance alone cannot identify a specific historical officer.

latest_context_review.finding: Benin's local use of imported materials is not reduced to European meanings. Rank or office cannot be read off an object without contextual support.

glossary_audits.name: material culture
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Everyday things and prestige objects both fit. The example of a drum uses making, use and social relations rather than metal alone.

latest_context_review.finding: The assigned objects include ordinary and prestigious things. The category does not make stylistic resemblance proof of a shared language, people or state.

glossary_audits.name: enslavement
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The definition makes coercion and denial of freedom explicit. Its use in Banda and Atlantic contexts should not be extended to every form of dependent labor.

latest_context_review.finding: Kongo letters distinguish free people and captives rather than claiming universal abolition. Haiti distinguishes emancipation from free movement at work; Cherokee slavery has its own political history.

glossary_audits.name: colonialism
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Outside power and unequal relations fit Banda and Saint-Domingue. An imported object by itself would be insufficient to identify colonial rule.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned colonial encounters retain distinct institutions and dates. The Portuguese voyage is not presented as creating an otherwise nonexistent Indian Ocean trading world.

glossary_audits.name: decolonization
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The plural “processes” fits Ghana, Indonesia and Partition. Political handover can be dated separately from changes to local power and inequality.

latest_context_review.finding: India/Pakistan, Indonesia, Ghana and South Africa have different political chronologies. The definition's process and inequality qualifications avoid treating independence or a constitution as completion of every transformation.

glossary_audits.name: archive
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Keeping, losing and providing access help explain the surviving Banda and Warsaw records. A gap in a collection cannot show that an event never happened.

latest_context_review.finding: Banda's missing Bandanese voices, Partition's later testimony and the Oneg Shabbat archive make selection and survival visible. An institutional archive name does not make its records neutral or exhaustive.

glossary_audits.name: industrialization
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Skill and work organization appear beside machines and energy, making this applicable to Tomioka as well as British factories. Different timings remain explicit.

latest_context_review.finding: Factory reform, Hine and Tomioka retain local workplaces, law and labor histories. No universal European timetable is imposed.

glossary_audits.name: earthwork
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Mounds and enclosures at Poverty Point and Hopewell fit the definition; neither shape nor size alone identifies their builders’ government.

latest_context_review.finding: Poverty Point construction phases and Hopewell research labels remain separate from purpose or constitutional claims. An earthwork's form is insufficient to identify its builders' political system.

glossary_audits.name: terminus post quem
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Replaced a vague “limit after which” with the earliest possible date supported by evidence. The example dates the use of the specific timber and allows storage and reuse.

latest_context_review.finding: The Ocmulgee and Laine timber examples distinguish last surviving growth from construction, allowing reuse or storage. An earliest possible date is not an exact construction date.

glossary_audits.name: calibration
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: A reference curve and several possible calendar dates account for the Wendat graph. Calibration is distinguished from simply subtracting a radiocarbon age from a year.

latest_context_review.finding: Laine's alternative calendar placements are retained. A calibrated date is not generated by treating radiocarbon years as a straight calendar conversion.

glossary_audits.name: syllabary
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Signs represent syllables, which explains why the Cherokee page has its own writing system. The definition does not imply that a bilingual page was readable by everyone.

latest_context_review.finding: The Cherokee writing system is named as Cherokee, not an adaptation of English spelling or ornamental symbols. The Nation's history identifies Sequoyah's system and later Cherokee-language print.

glossary_audits.name: wampum
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Onondaga account supplies situated meanings of belts and speakers. Recognizing shell beads does not permit an observer to assign a belt’s message independently.

latest_context_review.finding: Onondaga's own account identifies worked shell, speaking, agreements, memory and responsibilities. The definition does not reduce wampum to currency or claim a design speaks without knowledgeable people.

glossary_audits.name: ratification
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Separates negotiation, signature and formal confirmation in Canandaigua. The text does not equate ratification with fulfillment of promises.

latest_context_review.finding: The Canandaigua record distinguishes the 1794 treaty and the 1795 ratification instrument. Formal confirmation is not proof of equal consent, fulfillment or extinguishment of all claims.

glossary_audits.name: manoomin
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Ojibwe name remains connected with food, cultural and spiritual significance. Naming the community accounts avoids claiming identical practices throughout the region.

latest_context_review.finding: GLIFWC names a relationship of reciprocal care and cultural and spiritual significance. The term does not determine a photographed person's identity, a specific lake or an individual's treaty rights.

glossary_audits.name: winnowing
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Separation of grain from lighter chaff fits the Commission’s finishing sequence, distinct from other postharvest steps.

latest_context_review.finding: GLIFWC distinguishes drying, parching, hulling and winnowing. The definition describes separation from chaff rather than treating all rice finishing as one action.

glossary_audits.name: marine reservoir effect
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The comparison is between marine and contemporary terrestrial carbon; the need for local corrections is meaningful for the Bering Sea case.

latest_context_review.finding: The Bering Sea dossier distinguishes marine carbon and regional corrections from a museum object's existing catalogue range. No automatic redating of individual carvings follows.

glossary_audits.name: reconstruction
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The modern Hidatsa lodge and Inuinnait parkas show different uses of earlier evidence. Modern construction has its own date even when representing past practices.

latest_context_review.finding: Inuinnait modern reconstructions, Ocmulgee's rebuilt shelter and other interpretive reconstructions are not silently identified as original surviving fabric or ancient events.

glossary_audits.name: radiocarbon
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Once-living material, calibration and environmental effects anchor the method in sampled remains. The caution about BP matters at Ozette.

latest_context_review.finding: Ozette's reported years BP and Ocmulgee's revised timber analysis require calibration and sample context. The short definition does not assign one calendar date to all associated objects.

glossary_audits.name: waterlogged preservation
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Slow decay under persistently wet conditions explains why wood can survive at Ozette. The wording leaves room for selective survival.

latest_context_review.finding: Ozette's wet deposits explain selective survival. They do not represent a complete household or imply that preservation stops every kind of deterioration.

glossary_audits.name: seasonal round
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Organized movements and activities across a year fit the Blackfoot landscape. Mobility is treated as work requiring knowledge rather than an absence of institutions.

latest_context_review.finding: Blackfoot activities and mobility are treated as organized knowledge and work, not absence of institutions. The term remains bounded by the named community example.

glossary_audits.name: cache pit
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: An underground storage space connects Hidatsa agriculture to storage. An illustrative model cannot establish the contents of a particular excavated pit.

latest_context_review.finding: The Hidatsa storage example distinguishes interpreted construction and use from a present explanatory model. The plural case wording remains word-list accessible without automatic stemming.

glossary_audits.name: repatriation
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Return is situated in the account of Kwakwaka’wakw belongings. The definition encompasses ancestral remains without implying they are interchangeable with objects.

latest_context_review.finding: U'mista describes particular confiscations, returns and custody. The definition does not impose a single statutory route, promise all items have returned, or adjudicate another collection's ownership.

glossary_audits.name: potlatch
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Witnessing and gifts are introduced through the named Kwakwaka’wakw account. Variation across Northwest Coast communities is explicit.

latest_context_review.finding: U'mista's own account makes invited people witnesses and explains gifts and consequential occasions. The definition expressly allows different Northwest Coast community forms.

glossary_audits.name: experimental archaeology
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Stated conditions and a possible method fit the bison-processing experiment. The reader can distinguish experimental materials from an excavated event.

latest_context_review.finding: Replication tests possibilities in Egyptian, Poverty Point and Blackfoot examples. A successful experiment is not proof that an unobserved ancient event occurred identically.

glossary_audits.name: archaeological tradition
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Shared material practices can be grouped across sites; a Hopewell or Bering Sea label alone cannot identify a state, language or unified nation.

latest_context_review.finding: Hopewell and Bering Sea research labels do not automatically name a single enduring people, language or state. Current community relationships remain separately attributed.

glossary_audits.name: biomarker
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The chemical-trace example fits the Chaco vessel inquiry. It requires a stated sample and alternative explanations before reconstructing a drink or practice.

latest_context_review.finding: Chaco's theobromine result is interpreted at the scale of sampled vessels and analytical methods, not as an unrestricted claim about every resident's diet.

glossary_audits.name: kiva
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Pueblo context and variable form distinguish a cultural identification from a plan shape. A circular feature alone remains insufficient.

latest_context_review.finding: The Chaco definition allows varied forms and histories. NPS describes several ceremonial and social uses; no restricted community knowledge is invented, and circular shape alone is not a universal meaning.

glossary_audits.name: proxy
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The lake-sediment example translates an indirect observation into everyday language. A changing signal does not count individual Cahokia residents.

latest_context_review.finding: Cahokia's sediment signal remains indirect evidence. It cannot become a direct census or erase other evidence of environmental pressure.

glossary_audits.name: chiefdom
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The Cahokia entry identifies an analytical interpretation of ranked leadership. Neither an official title nor institutional unanimity follows from the term.

latest_context_review.finding: The Cahokia term remains an analytical interpretation, not a recovered official title or a synonym for every Indigenous polity. No identical governance is assigned to all mounds.

glossary_audits.name: stonepaste
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Quartz, clay and glassy material distinguish the Iznik ceramic body from porcelain. The definition does not purport to provide the selected dish’s recipe.

latest_context_review.finding: The Met's technical description supports quartz with glass and clay. Iznik stonepaste is kept distinct from porcelain despite shared visual motifs.

glossary_audits.name: tughra
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: An Ottoman sultan’s emblem can involve calligraphy and decoration; the definition permits multiple skilled participants. It does not attribute the drawing to the sultan personally.

latest_context_review.finding: The Met's object record distinguishes the standard emblem's drafter from its illuminator. The definition concerns Ottoman authority without equating all calligraphy with the sultan's signature.

glossary_audits.name: forced relocation
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Coercion is explicit in the New Julfa and Cherokee cases. Later adaptation or success is kept separate from the conditions of removal.

latest_context_review.finding: New Julfa and Cherokee removal are separately situated. Later institutions, rights or achievements are not used to make coerced movement voluntary.

glossary_audits.name: caravansary
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Merchants, goods and an establishment make this more specific than a route. The term accommodates both urban and overland settings.

latest_context_review.finding: Isfahan and Bukhara's commercial establishments are contextual examples, not one fixed plan or proof that an individual merchant stayed there.

glossary_audits.name: madrasa
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Learning institutions vary across Islamic societies. Bukhara’s surviving building requires further evidence for the curriculum or an individual student’s experience.

latest_context_review.finding: Bukhara's institutional and architectural account includes student cells, teaching and a mosque. MIT's architectural record corroborates this layout; the definition does not prescribe one curriculum for all Islamic societies.

glossary_audits.name: lacquer
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The protective finish is distinguished from the painted papier-mâché and pasteboard support in the Iranian dressing case. No chemical recipe is inferred.

latest_context_review.finding: The selected Iranian object is painted, lacquered papier-mâché and pasteboard. The definition does not import a Chinese or Japanese tree-resin recipe into this case.

glossary_audits.name: sovereignty
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Proclamation, foreign recognition and effective control can be investigated separately. This matters particularly for Indonesia’s 1945, 1949 and 1950 milestones.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned only to Indonesia and Ghana. Declaration, Dutch transfer and control have distinct histories. Te Tiriti's kāwanatanga and tino rangatiratanga remain in attributed passage explanations instead of being auto-linked to a single state-sovereignty definition.

glossary_audits.name: federation
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Divided powers, subject to a particular agreement, fits the Indonesian settlement and Ghanaian debates. It does not imply equal power at each level.

latest_context_review.finding: Indonesia's proposed and short-lived federal arrangements and Ghana's regional-power proposal remain distinct. Mention of a federation does not establish that the same constitution was adopted in both places.

glossary_audits.name: Standardization
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The distinction between an announced standard and observed practice fits Qin measures. A rule does not establish immediate or universal adoption.

latest_context_review.finding: Qin prescribed form is distinguished from practical variation. Announcement of standard rules is not evidence of uniform implementation.

glossary_audits.name: Dhamma
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The term is explicitly attached to Ashoka’s messages on conduct and government. It avoids treating a selected edict as an exhaustive account of Buddhist belief.

latest_context_review.finding: The Ashoka case explicitly attributes the moral/administrative interpretation to Neelis and distinguishes it from all Buddhist doctrine. This case-specific gloss is not a definition of every use of dharma/dhamma.

glossary_audits.name: Deme
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The local Attic community and a specified fourth-century account prevent confusion with citizenship in any modern municipality. Enrollment is attributed to eligible men.

latest_context_review.finding: The late-fourth-century Athenian account's enrollment and scrutiny requirements are kept dated. The definition does not call all residents citizens or project one procedure onto all Greek communities.

glossary_audits.name: Stratigraphy
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Relationships between layers and features explain why a deposit and its contents may have different dates. This applies to the Aksum and Caral examples.

latest_context_review.finding: Deposit relationships and manufacture dates remain distinct in Aksum, Caral, Olmec, Lapita and Poverty Point. Layers do not automatically supply an object's exact original use date.

glossary_audits.name: Endowment
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Property or other resources can sustain an institution over time. At Nalanda, terms and maintenance require evidence beyond the surviving building.

latest_context_review.finding: Nalanda's institutional support and the work supplying it need separate evidence. The general word does not equate all endowments with one legal institution such as waqf.

glossary_audits.name: Mit’a
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Rotating service is distinguished from resettlement. Food supplied to Inca workers does not in itself measure how much choice they had.

latest_context_review.finding: NMAI describes periodic state labor in the Inka setting. The dossier separately names mitmaqkuna resettlement; the gloss is not automatically applied to later colonial mita or voluntary reciprocal help.

glossary_audits.name: Jeli / jeliw
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The definition identifies the plural jeliw and includes multiple Mande performance roles. A particular performance retains its own audience and date.

latest_context_review.finding: The Met's Epics section explicitly gives jeli/jeliw and multiple Mande specialist roles. Performance date, audience and living adaptation are retained rather than treating every version as a literal transcript of medieval events.

glossary_audits.name: Provisioning
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Storage, preparation and delivery translate an abstract word into identifiable tasks. Egyptian and Moche cases can then be compared without assuming identical administration.

latest_context_review.finding: Administrative records, production and distribution explain different tasks. The term does not establish how every worker was recruited or how fairly supplies were shared.

glossary_audits.name: Shicra
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: A woven plant-fiber bag is concrete; stone-filled examples belong specifically to Caral deposits. Bags cannot identify a labor obligation unaided.

latest_context_review.finding: Caral explicitly identifies a woven plant-fiber bag and stone-filled construction deposits. The bags do not reveal the recruitment, obligations or choices of every builder.

glossary_audits.name: Midden
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Discarded material and layered occupation deposits are both intelligible at Skara Brae and Poverty Point. A midden requires its own formation history and dating.

latest_context_review.finding: Skara Brae's accumulated material and Poverty Point deposits retain chronology and context. Refuse accumulation is not an automatic count of an entire settlement's population.

glossary_audits.name: Temper
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Added non-clay material affects how pottery behaves. The Lapita case can consider material sources without inferring a named carrier or complete voyage.

latest_context_review.finding: Lapita's non-clay inclusions are examined as material evidence. A nonlocal temper interpretation does not by itself identify who transported a pot or whether raw ingredients moved.

glossary_audits.name: Type-site
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Naming a category after a place differs from proving that the practice originated or spread from there. This distinction is directly relevant to Poverty Point.

latest_context_review.finding: Poverty Point supplies a research category's name; the dossier expressly leaves independent dates and directions of transmission open.

glossary_audits.name: LiDAR
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Light pulses and elevation modeling explain how ground shapes become visible. Neither the model nor an observed mound supplies a construction date.

latest_context_review.finding: The Poverty Point terrain model makes surface forms visible while excavation and dating address their histories. Elevation measurement is not itself a construction date.

glossary_audits.name: Faience
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Quartz-rich glazed material is distinguishable from granite and ordinary clay. The Taharqo inquiry also needs object-specific evidence of manufacture.

latest_context_review.finding: Taharqo's Sanam quartz-rich production remains separate from the selected granite shabti and from ordinary clay ceramic bodies. European tin-glazed earthenware meanings are not attached to this assignment.

glossary_audits.name: Shabti
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: The figure’s intended funerary work is clear. The words “intended” and “royal example” leave particular objects and beliefs open to specific investigation.

latest_context_review.finding: The royal funerary figure and Sanam production debris are different objects and contexts. Expected service after death does not establish all households' beliefs or all figures' materials.

glossary_audits.name: Plain weave
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Added the reversal on the next row. The crosswise and lengthwise terms now allow the learner to follow both directions in the Chavín teaching diagram.

latest_context_review.finding: The educational weave diagram illustrates a method. It is not a technical analysis proving the selected Chavín textile has that weave.

glossary_audits.name: Residential compound
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Connected rooms and open spaces can support multiple activities. At Teotihuacan the structure alone does not identify the size or legal status of a household.

latest_context_review.finding: Teotihuacan and Moche compounds can combine living, production, storage and gathering. Architectural boundaries alone do not prove a nuclear household or legal status.

glossary_audits.name: Find context
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Place, surrounding material and association distinguish archaeological context from style, ownership or museum location. This applies to the Colima figures.

latest_context_review.finding: Precise discovery associations are distinct from regional style, modern museum location and an ownership history. This remains compatible with the corrected provenance entry.

glossary_audits.name: Relief
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Forms projecting from a background give a visible test applicable at Borobudur. The representation still requires evidence for use and interpretation.

latest_context_review.finding: Assigned only to art/architecture in Byzantium and Borobudur. Exact matching avoids unrelated humanitarian meanings and does not automatically stem reliefs into a link.

glossary_audits.name: Iconoclasm
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Opposition can extend to destruction but takes different forms. The Byzantine entry attaches disputes to specific periods and policies.

latest_context_review.finding: The Byzantine setting is dated and qualified. Opposition to images is not attributed to every Christian, period or institution.

glossary_audits.name: Masonry
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Stone, bricks and different components of a wall are concrete. The Chaco construction does not identify its builders’ identities or governance by material alone.

latest_context_review.finding: Chaco's rubble cores, facing and later conservation require separate evidence. Visible masonry does not identify every original builder or establish that all exposed fabric is ancient.

glossary_audits.name: Workshop
glossary_audits.contextual_variation: Both a setting and a group of workers are possible. Catalogue attribution to an Ottoman or Mughal workshop supplies neither a roster nor ownership on its own.

latest_context_review.finding: Ming, Mughal and Ottoman production settings differ in scale and control. A catalogue attribution does not recover all makers, labor conditions or the complete organizational history.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Communities, cities and the evidence of work
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Separate a visible mark from an inferred purpose.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Compare how records and buildings reveal cooperation while leaving people out.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Describe one mark without translating it; identify one thing an account leaves out.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Networks, resources and disruption
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Distinguish what was found together from an inferred origin.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Explain a network using evidence while leaving an unsupported itinerary open.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Name two recovered materials, then distinguish their discovery from the analysis needed to infer origins.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: States, ideas and everyday voices
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Separate a visible detail from an interpretation supplied by a source.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Compare how different evidence represents authority and whose voices are missing.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Point to one visible feature and identify the museum explanation needed for a claim about purpose.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Contemporary worlds
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Use a model to identify a household need and an omitted task.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Compare contemporary cases without inferring contact from overlapping dates.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Link a tower, granary or well to a need, and name someone or some work the model does not show.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Communities and institutions in transition
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Sort an observation, a source interpretation and an unsupported claim.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Explain how an institution and a surviving object have different historical scopes.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Identify a visible feature; separate the proposed use from an imagined journey of the particular object.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Cities, craft and knowledge in motion
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Explain how a royal image makes some work visible and leaves other work out.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Connect movement and knowledge through named intermediaries while keeping evidence limits explicit.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Describe one royal symbol and one everyday task absent from the image; say what other evidence would be needed.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Connections, work and unequal power
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Name work and knowledge required for an arrival beyond sailing.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Explain exchange and unequal power through specific intermediaries and dated encounters.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Identify a pilot, supplies or conversation and distinguish a schematic connection from an exact ship track.

chapter_learning_contracts.title: Industry, empire and struggles over the future
chapter_learning_contracts.short_activity_outcome: Sequence distinct statements about status, work and independence.
chapter_learning_contracts.deeper_route_outcome: Compare the promises and constraints of changing systems of work and political authority.
chapter_learning_contracts.facilitator_rubric: Separate the 1801 legal/work provisions from the 1804 political decision and identify whose agreement the later text records.
